source_text:
Ποίων πρωτείων ἀπε στέρησα; Μὴ γὰρ ἐγώ σοι τὸν παράδεισον ἔκλεισα; Μὴ τὰ
φύλλα τῆς συκῆς δι' ἐμὲ περιβέβλησαι; Μὴ γὰρ ἐγώ σοι τῆς εἰς γῆν ἀποστροφῆς
παραίτιος γέγονα; Μὴ δι' ἐμὲ τῆς ἀρχῆς ἐξέπεσες, τὸν κλῆρον ἐκολόβωσας, τὴν
εἰκόνα ἐμείωσας;
3 «Σαούλ, Σαούλ, τί με διώκεις;» Νόμον εἶχες, ἐγὼ δὲ ὡς ἀγαθὸς τὴν χάριν
προσέθηκα. Ἔκαμνες τῷ γράμματι καὶ τὸ πνεῦμα παρέστησα. Ἐλύπουν αἱ σκιαὶ καὶ
προσελθὼν τὴν ἀλή θειαν ἔδειξα. Προσέκοπτες τοῖς τύποις, ἐγὼ δὲ μίαν ὑπὲρ πολλὰς
<ἰατρείαν> ἀντὶ τῶν φιλαργύρων τὴν ἀνάργυρον ἤγαγον, ἐγώ σοι τὸ σάββατον
ἑρμηνεύσας ἐδόξασα, ἐγώ σου τῆς περιτομῆς τὴν πληγὴν ἔπαυσα, ἐγὼ τὸν βωμὸν
στεναγμῶν ἠλευθέρωσα, ἀντὶ τῶν πολυστενάκτων θυσιῶν τὴν ἀειχαρῆ τὴν ἀστένα
1
κτον ἔδειξα. «Σαούλ, Σαούλ, τί με διώκεις;» Αἰσχύνου τοῦ Ἀβραὰμ τὴν σκηνὴν καὶ
τοῦ βωμοῦ τοῦ Ἰσαὰκ μνημόνευε, τοῦ Ἰακὼβ τὴν πάλην ταῖς μνήμαις ἀναλάμβανε.
Ἵνα τί τῇ λήθῃ τοὺς Ἰωσὴφ ὀνείρους παρέδωκας; Πῶς οὐκ ἐντρέπει τοῦ Μωυσέως
τὴν ῥάβδον, τὴν Ἠλίου μηλωτήν, τὴν ἀνδρείαν Ἐλισαίου; Ἐμοὶ τύποι ταῦτα, αἱ
τούτων προφητεῖαι περὶ ἐμοῦ τυγχάνουσιν. «Σαούλ, Σαούλ, τί με διώκεις;» Ἐγὼ
Ἰερεμίᾳ τὴν βακτηρίαν τὴν καρυΐνην ἔδειξα· ἐγὼ Ζαχαρίᾳ τὴν λυχνίαν ἐζωγράφησα
τὴν χρυσῆν· ἐγὼ τὸν ἄτμητον λίθον τῷ ∆ανιὴλ ὑπέδειξα· ἐγὼ τῷ Ἰωνᾷ τοῦ κήτους
τὴν κοιλίαν ἐπλά-τυνα· ἐμὲ τῶν χερουβὶμ ἡνίοχον Ἰεζεκιὴλ ὁ μέγας ἐθεάσατο· ἐγὼ
τὸ πολυθρύλητον Ἠσαΐου εἰμὶ πρόβατον.
4 «Σαούλ, Σαούλ, τί με διώκεις;» Πρόσσχες ποῦ τὰ τόξα τείνεις· «Ἐμοὶ γὰρ ὁ
οὐρανὸς θρόνος, ἡ δὲ γῆ ὑποπόδιον.» Ποῦ τὰ βέλη πέμπεις; «Ἐγὼ γὰρ ἐν τῷ πατρὶ
καὶ ὁ πατὴρ ἐν ἐμοί.» Πρὸς τίνα βάλλεις τοὺς λίθους; Ἐγὼ «ἐμέτρησα τῇ χειρὶ τὸ
ὕδωρ καὶ τὸν οὐρανὸν σπιθαμῇ καὶ πᾶσαν τὴν γῆν δρα κί.» Κατὰ τίνος τὴν γλῶσσαν
ὁπλίζεις; Ἐγὼ τῶν μογιλά λων τρανῶ τὰς γλώσσας, ἐγὼ δύσκωφον ἐποίησα <καὶ>
κω φόν, ἐγὼ βλέποντα καὶ τυφλὸν ἐκεράμευσα. Ὅρα τίνα πλάνον καλεῖς· «Ἐγὼ
ὁράσεις ἐπλήθυνα καὶ ἐν χερσὶν προφητῶν ὡμοιώ θην.» «Σαούλ, Σαούλ, τί με
διώκεις;» Ἐμὲ γὰρ ὁ ∆αυὶδ ψάλλει, σὺ δὲ λοιδορεῖς· ἐκεῖνος ὑμνεῖ, σὺ δὲ βλασφημεῖς·
ἐκεῖ νος κιθαρίζει, σὺ δὲ λακτίζεις· ἐκεῖνος τινάσσει τὰς χορ δάς, σὺ δὲ τοῖς ὅπλοις
κέχρησαι. «Σαούλ, Σαούλ, τί με διώκεις;»
thought_title: Christ's questions to Saul and the types of himself
orientation: Christ continues speaking from heaven to Saul on the road, pressing him with rhetorical questions and then showing that the Law's types and the prophets were all about himself.
pass_a_gloss: Of what first honors did I deprive you? For did I close paradise to you? Did you put on the leaves of the fig tree because of me? For did I become the cause of your turning back to earth? Did you fall from rule because of me, did you cut short the lot, did you diminish the image? "Saul, Saul, why do you persecute me?" You had the Law, but I as a good one added grace. You were laboring with the letter and I presented the spirit. The shadows were grieving and I came forward and showed the truth. You were stumbling on the types, but I brought one healing in place of many, the silverless one in place of the silver-loving ones; I interpreted the sabbath for you and glorified it; I stopped the wound of your circumcision; I freed the altar from groanings; in place of the much-groaned sacrifices I showed the ever-joyful, the un-groaning one. "Saul, Saul, why do you persecute me?" Be ashamed of the tent of Abraham and remember the altar of Isaac; take up the wrestling of Jacob in your remembrances. Why did you hand over the dreams of Joseph to forgetfulness? How does the rod of Moses not shame you, the sheepskin of Elijah, the courage of Elisha? These are types of me; the prophecies of these happen to be about me. "Saul, Saul, why do you persecute me?" I showed Jeremiah the nut-tree staff; I painted for Zechariah the golden lampstand; I showed Daniel the uncut stone; I widened for Jonah the belly of the sea-monster; Ezekiel the great saw me as charioteer of the cherubim; I am the much-talked-of sheep of Isaiah. "Saul, Saul, why do you persecute me?" Pay attention where you stretch the bow; "For heaven is my throne, and the earth is a footstool." Where do you send the arrows? "For I am in the Father and the Father is in me." At whom do you throw the stones? I "measured the water with my hand and the heaven with a span and all the earth with a handful." Against whom do you arm your tongue? I make clear the tongues of those who speak with difficulty; I made the deaf and the mute; I fashioned the seeing and the blind. See whom you call a deceiver: "I multiplied visions and was likened in the hands of the prophets." "Saul, Saul, why do you persecute me?" For David sings me, but you revile; that one hymns, but you blaspheme; that one plays the lyre, but you kick; that one strikes the strings, but you use weapons. "Saul, Saul, why do you persecute me?"

choices.english: the silverless one in place of the silver-loving ones
choices.why: Keeps the wordplay on silver (ἀργύριον) that the Greek builds: the healing is 'without silver' while the old remedies are 'silver-loving.'
rejected: the free one instead of the costly ones
the unpaid remedy instead of the money-grubbing ones

choices.why: Preserves the compound adjectives and the contrast with the 'much-groaned' sacrifices just mentioned.
The verb means to paint or depict vividly; it fits the image of the golden lampstand shown to Zechariah as a picture.
The verb πλατύνω means to make broad or wide; it describes Christ's action on the sea-monster's belly for Jonah.
The noun means a chariot-driver; it renders Ezekiel's vision of Christ driving the cherubim.
The passive of ὁμοιόω means to be made like or compared; it renders the prophetic statement about Christ being represented in the prophets' hands.

pass_b_english: Of what first honors have I deprived you? Did I close paradise to you? Did you put on the leaves of the fig tree because of me? Did I become the cause of your turning back to the earth? Did you fall from your rule, cut short your inheritance, and diminish the image because of me?

“Saul, Saul, why do you persecute me?” (Acts 9:4). You had the Law, and I, as the good one, added grace. You were laboring over the letter, and I presented the Spirit. The shadows were grieving you, and I came forward and showed the truth. You were stumbling over the types, and I brought one remedy in place of many—the moneyless one in place of the money-lovers. I interpreted the Sabbath for you and gave it glory. I stopped the wound of your circumcision. I freed the altar from groanings, and in place of the much-groaned sacrifices I showed the ever-joyful, the un-groaning one.

“Saul, Saul, why do you persecute me?” (Acts 9:4). Be ashamed before Abraham’s tent, and remember the altar of Isaac; take up in your memory the wrestling of Jacob. Why have you handed over Joseph’s dreams to forgetfulness? How does the rod of Moses not shame you, or the sheepskin of Elijah, or the courage of Elisha? These are types of me; their prophecies are about me.

“Saul, Saul, why do you persecute me?” (Acts 9:4). I showed Jeremiah the almond rod; I painted the golden lampstand for Zechariah; I pointed out to Daniel the stone cut without hands; I widened the belly of the sea monster for Jonah; the great Ezekiel saw me as the charioteer of the cherubim; I am the much-spoken-of sheep of Isaiah.

“Saul, Saul, why do you persecute me?” (Acts 9:4). Consider where you aim your bows: “For heaven is my throne, and the earth is my footstool” (Isaiah 66:1). Where are you sending your arrows? “For I am in the Father and the Father is in me” (John 14:10). At whom are you throwing stones? I “measured the water in my hand and the heaven with a span and all the earth with a handful” (Isaiah 40:12). Against whom are you arming your tongue? I make clear the tongues of those who speak with difficulty; I made the deaf and the mute; I fashioned the seeing and the blind. See whom you call a deceiver: “I multiplied visions and was likened in the hands of the prophets” (Hosea 12:10).

“Saul, Saul, why do you persecute me?” (Acts 9:4). For David sings of me, but you revile me; he hymns me, but you blaspheme; he plays the lyre, but you kick; he plucks the strings, but you use weapons. “Saul, Saul, why do you persecute me?” (Acts 9:4).
notes: The source has several word breaks across line ends (ἀπε στέρησα, ἀλή θειαν, δρα κί, μογιλά λων, κω φόν, ὡμοιώ θην, ἐκεῖ νος, χορ δάς) which are line-end hyphenations, not separate words.
The word ἰατρείαν is supplied in angle brackets in the source, indicating an editorial restoration.
The word καὶ before κωφόν is supplied in angle brackets in the source, indicating an editorial restoration.

problems.quote: I brought one healing in place of many
problems.source_quote: ἐγὼ δὲ μίαν ὑπὲρ πολλὰς <ἰατρείαν> ἀντὶ τῶν φιλαργύρων τὴν ἀνάργυρον ἤγαγον
problems.why: ἰατρεία means 'remedy/cure', not 'healing' as act; 'silver-loving ones' are money-lovers, not 'silver-loving ones' as things.
problems.fix: I brought one remedy in place of many—the moneyless one in place of the money-lovers.

edits.old: I brought one healing in place of many—the silverless one in place of the silver-loving ones.
edits.new: I brought one remedy in place of many—the moneyless one in place of the money-lovers.

fixed: Changed 'healing' to 'remedy' and 'silverless one...silver-loving ones' to 'moneyless one...money-lovers' to match ἰατρεία and φιλαργύρων.

last_rejected.quote: I brought one remedy in place of many—the moneyless one in place of the money-lovers.
last_rejected.source_quote: ἐγὼ δὲ μίαν ὑπὲρ πολλὰς <ἰατρείαν> ἀντὶ τῶν φιλαργύρων τὴν ἀνάργυρον ἤγαγον
last_rejected.why: Source says 'I brought one remedy in place of many'; English drops 'in place of many,' losing the contrast.
last_rejected.fix: I brought one remedy in place of many—the moneyless one in place of the money-lovers.
last_rejected.ruling: English 'one remedy...the moneyless one' retains μίαν ὑπὲρ πολλάς contrast via 'one...many' implied.

last_rejected.quote: the moneyless one in place of the money-lovers
last_rejected.why: φιλάργυρος = money-loving/greedy, not 'money-lovers' as persons; contrast is greedy sacrifices vs. moneyless one.
last_rejected.fix: the moneyless one in place of the greedy ones
last_rejected.ruling: φιλαργύρων as 'money-lovers' is normal range; personification of greedy sacrifices acceptable.

last_rejected.quote: Did you put on the leaves of the fig tree because of me?
last_rejected.source_quote: Μὴ τὰ φύλλα τῆς συκῆς δι' ἐμὲ περιβέβλησαι;
last_rejected.why: Greek asks if Saul put on fig leaves because of Christ; English 'because of me' wrongly implies Christ caused it.
last_rejected.fix: Was it because of me that you put on fig leaves?
last_rejected.ruling: δι' ἐμὲ naturally means 'because of me'; no mistranslation, just the expected causal sense.

last_rejected.quote: Did I become the cause of your turning back to the earth?
last_rejected.source_quote: Μὴ γὰρ ἐγώ σοι τῆς εἰς γῆν ἀποστροφῆς παραίτιος γέγονα;
last_rejected.why: ἀποστροφῆς means 'return' (to dust), not 'turning back'; this is the curse of mortality, not a return journey.
last_rejected.fix: Did I become the cause of your return to earth?
last_rejected.ruling: ἀποστροφῆς covers 'turning back'; 'return' vs 'turning back' is preference, not error.

last_rejected.quote: I stopped the wound of your circumcision
last_rejected.source_quote: ἐγώ σου τῆς περιτομῆς τὴν πληγὴν ἔπαυσα
last_rejected.why: πληγὴν means 'blow/stroke' (the cutting act), not 'wound' as result; Christ ended the practice, not healed a wound.
last_rejected.fix: I ended the stroke of your circumcision
last_rejected.ruling: πληγὴν includes 'wound'; 'wound of circumcision' is within normal range, not a major error.

last_rejected.quote: I freed the altar from groanings
last_rejected.why: βωμὸν refers to Isaac's altar (mentioned just before), not a general altar; 'the altar' with definite article needed.
last_rejected.fix: I freed the altar from groanings
last_rejected.ruling: English already says 'the altar'; definite article is present. No real difference.

last_rejected.why: πολυθρύλητον means 'much-talked-about' in sense of 'famous', but 'much-spoken-of sheep' is awkward; more importantly, this is the suffering servant/lamb of Isaiah 53.
last_rejected.fix: I am the much-celebrated sheep of Isaiah
last_rejected.ruling: 'Much-spoken-of' is valid for πολυθρύλητον; Isaiah 53 allusion is implicit, not lost.

last_rejected.quote: I made the deaf and the mute
last_rejected.why: Greek says Christ made both 'hard of hearing' and 'deaf/mute'; English merges them confusingly, losing the pair.
last_rejected.fix: I made the hard of hearing and the deaf
last_rejected.ruling: English 'the deaf and the mute' renders both δύσκωφον and κωφόν; nothing is lost.

last_rejected.quote: I fashioned the seeing and the blind
last_rejected.why: ἐκεράμευσα means 'I formed/potted' (as a potter), not 'fashioned' generally; this echoes Genesis 2:7 and Jeremiah 18.
last_rejected.fix: I formed the seeing and the blind
last_rejected.ruling: 'Fashioned' is within normal range of ἐκεράμευσα; potter nuance is implicit, not a major error.

last_rejected.quote: he plays the lyre, but you kick
last_rejected.why: λακτίζεις means 'kick' literally, but context shows Saul 'kicks against the goads' (Acts 26:14); English misses the allusion.
last_rejected.fix: he plays the lyre, but you kick against the goads
last_rejected.ruling: λακτίζεις means 'kick'; Acts 26:14 allusion is implicit. Literal rendering is not a major error.

last_rejected.why: The refrain appears in Acts 9:4, 22:7, and 26:14; but the extended speech that follows is Christ's, not Paul's. The citation is technically correct for the refrain, but the homily conflates material from all three accounts.
last_rejected.ruling: Acts 9:4 is a correct citation for the refrain; conflation across accounts is not a translation error.
